newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes advance ahead of June paper expiry.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes advance ahead of June paper expiry.

text.p: Cash crude prices regained strength Tuesday after suffering widespread selling on Monday, mainly reflecting the uncertainty ahead of NYMEX expiry.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing gained around five cents to $21.60-70 a barrel, following morning losses.
June/July spreads retreated to around 35 cents, allowing a corresponding uptick in Postings Plus business. Traders said deals were done for Postings at $1.80, from $1.75 on Monday.

For other grades, Midland sweet barrels traded slightly weaker at WTI/Cushing -41 cents, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James selling at even and two cents weaker to benchmark, steady to firmer than Monday discussion.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold at a $1.40 discount to WTI/Cushing, in the middle of ranges traded yesterday.
Players said June NYMEX expiry was the feature at play in today's market, especially the question of how much foreign crude is delivered against the contract.
In May, 2.73 million barrels of Brent, Oseberg and Bonny Light were delivered, taking advantage of favorable economics.
Traders said some of those Bonny Light barrels may be pushed onto uninterested refiners again this month, again to take advantage of a 60 cents premium allocated by NYMEX for the Nigerian sweet.
"We're all in the dark on this, we'll find out later in the week how much found its way in," said a cash dealer.
Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) were tracked out to a very firm 20 cents in the morning, but have since been pegged around 14-16 cents.

EFPs, which allow a buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for physical positions, have been fetching firm premiums in recent weeks as traders work to escape paper psoitions that might give them a crude other than the benchmark WTI/Cushing once June futures expire.
